page: UpCloud PREMIUM-16xCPU-32GB is a premium-class virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor. The configuration provides 16 shared vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with 1 thread per core, operating at a base speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding 2.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 300 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores falling within the average range. Memory bandwidth is stable, showing average performance for both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block read/write operations. However, text generation for small LLM models is a notable bottleneck, registering in the bottom 10% of benchmarks, though medium model text generation remains average.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server offers a compute-focused resource density suitable for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. The inclusion of a 300 GB local SSD provides integrated storage without additional provisioning overhead. This instance is well-suited for workloads such as single-threaded data processing, software compilation, static web serving, and moderate database operations. It is less optimal for memory-intensive databases or large-scale LLM text generation.
description: UpCloud PREMIUM-16xCPU-32GB is a KVM-based virtual server configured with 16 shared vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 9575F processor and 32.0 GB of RAM. This x86_64 system includes a bundled 300 GB local SSD and one public IPv4 address, with no GPU hardware. Performance benchmarks highlight top-tier single-core capabilities, particularly in single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, while multi-core compute, memory bandwidth, and database operations perform at average levels. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio positions this server as a compute-oriented option. It is best suited for single-threaded processing, software compilation, static web serving, and moderate database workloads where high single-core performance is prioritized over massive memory capacity.
